newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ENGLAND'S BECKHAM AND CAMPBELL IN CUP DUEL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ENGLAND'S BECKHAM AND CAMPBELL IN CUP DUEL.

text.p: David Beckham and Sol Campbell are two young Londoners playing key roles for their clubs and becoming ever more important to England.
Beckham escaped the scouting net thrown around the capital by the London clubs to establish himself with Manchester United while Campbell has become crucial to the on-going development at Tottenham.
Born near each other in north-east London in the mid-1970s, they have both progressed a long way in a short time through the England youth, Under-21 and now full senior sides.
The last time they were on the same field as each other, they helped England to a 2-0 win over Georgia in a World Cup qualifying match.

On Sunday, barring injury or illness or Beckham being rested, they will both be at Old Trafford with very different objectives when holders Manchester United play Tottenham in the third round of the English F.A. Cup.

Beckham will be attempting to help United dominate the midfield, Campbell will be at the heart of Tottenham's defence - - and probably anywhere else he's needed -- as Spurs bid to keep their season alive with what, on current form, would be an unlikely victory.
But the fact that both young players -- Beckham is 21, Campbell is 22 -- should be seen as key players in the tie is testimony to the outstanding form they have both shown this season.

Beckham, who, like Campbell, won his third England cap against Georgia, began the season in truly sensational style when he scored with a shot from inside his own half in United's first league fixture against Wimbledon.
It immediately became one of the most famous goals ever scored in England and the fact it was no fluke says much about Beckham's ability and confidence despite his relative youth.
"I certainly meant to do it," he said. "I spotted the goalkeeper off his line and thought I might have a go. I was fortunate that I struck it well and it dipped at the right moment."
Beckham has continued to score regularly throughout the season and has established himself in the heart of the midfield, although his manager Alex Ferguson is determined to nurture him carefully.

He repeatedly says Beckham is a young player who needs a holiday or a rest, but that is easier said than done as United mount another serious challenge for the title, continue their quest for the European Cup and bid to become the first team ever to reach four successive F.A. Cup finals.
While Beckham has established himself in arguably the best side in the country Campbell has done the same in a team struggling to live up to Tottenham's past achievements.

Despite his comparative youth, Campbell has looked like a man among boys this season as Spurs have fallen out of the championship race, been knocked out of the League Cup 6-1 at Bolton and crushed 7-1 at Newcastle last week.
Manager Gerry Francis and unpopular chairman Alan Sugar have said Spurs are building a team capable of winning the title in three seasons time -- a claim that right now seems extremely fanciful.

After two seasons of using his strength and versatility in midfield and up front, Campbell is now established in the centre of defence where his perfectly-timed tackles have prevented Spurs conceding even more then the 26 league goals they have leaked already.
At 6ft 1ins (186 cm) and 14 stone, he is a towering presence in a side going through another disappointing "season of transition".

If they lose to United their season is effectively over, and it is not unreasonable to assume Campbell, tipped as a future England captain, might consider moving to a side capable of winning something.

"I am happy at Tottenham at the moment," he said in a recent interview. "It's been unbelievable so far and the fans have been good to me since I made my debut. I am here for the next few years and I am going to enjoy it. If it goes on from there, it goes on from there..."
Tottenham would be loathe to lose the man who on Sunday will present Beckham and company with their toughest obstacle on the road to the F.A. Cup fourth round.
